options.name: init_config
options.description: All options defined here are available to all instances.

options.name: proxy
options.description:
Set HTTP or HTTPS proxies for all instances. Use the `no_proxy` list
to specify hosts that must bypass proxies.

The SOCKS protocol is also supported like so:

  socks5://user:pass@host:port

Using the scheme `socks5` causes the DNS resolution to happen on the
client, rather than on the proxy server. This is in line with `curl`,
which uses the scheme to decide whether to do the DNS resolution on
the client or proxy. If you want to resolve the domains on the proxy
server, use `socks5h` as the scheme.

options.name: skip_proxy
options.description:
If set to `true`, this makes the check bypass any proxy
settings enabled and attempt to reach services directly.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The timeout for connecting to services.

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Additionally, this sets the default `service` for every log source.

options.name: instances
options.description: Every instance is scheduled independently of the others.

options.name: leader_election
options.description: Monitor the leader-election process on the kube-system:kube-controller-manager.

options.name: leader_election_kind
options.description:
The kind of object to look at for the leader election.

Options:
  * auto
  * lease
  * endpoints
  * configmap
The `auto` option makes the check try `lease` first and fallback to endpoints if `lease` isn't available.

options.name: health_url
options.description: The URL for the kube-controller-manager health endpoint.

options.name: ignore_deprecated
options.description: Filter deprecated metrics from the kube-controller-manager /metrics endpoints payload.

options.name: extra_queues
options.description:
Monitor additional queues, in addition to the default ones.
**NOTE**: `{WorkQueueName}_*` metrics were deprecated in Kubernetes v1.14 
in favor of `workqueue_*` metrics.

options.name: extra_limiters
options.description: Monitor additional rate limiters, in addition to the default ones.

options.name: prometheus_url
options.description: The URL where your application metrics are exposed by Prometheus.

options.name: prometheus_metrics_prefix
options.description: Removes a given <PREFIX> from exposed Prometheus metrics.

options.name: health_service_check
options.description:
Send a service check reporting about the health of the Prometheus endpoint.
The service check is named <NAMESPACE>.prometheus.health

options.name: label_to_hostname
options.description: Override the hostname with the value of one label.

options.name: label_joins
options.description: Allows targeting a metric to retrieve its label with a 1:1 mapping.

options.name: labels_mapper
options.description:
The label mapper allows you to rename labels.
Format is <LABEL_TO_RENAME>: <NEW_LABEL_NAME>

options.name: type_overrides
options.description:
Override a type in the Prometheus payload or type an untyped metric (ignored by default).
Supported <METRIC_TYPE> are `gauge`, `counter`, `histogram`, and `summary`.
The "*" wildcard can be used to match multiple metric names.

options.name: send_histograms_buckets
options.description: Set send_histograms_buckets to true to send the histograms bucket.

options.name: send_distribution_buckets
options.description:
Set `send_distribution_buckets` to `true` to send histograms as Datadog distribution metrics.

Learn more about distribution metrics: https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/metrics/distributions/

options.name: send_monotonic_counter
options.description: Set send_monotonic_counter to true to send counters as monotonic counter.

options.name: send_distribution_counts_as_monotonic
options.description: If set to true, sends histograms and summary counters as monotonic counters (instead of gauges).

options.name: send_distribution_sums_as_monotonic
options.description: If set to true, sends histograms and summary sums as monotonic counters (instead of gauges).

options.name: use_process_start_time
options.description:
Whether to enable a heuristic for reporting counter values on the first scrape. When true,
the first time an endpoint is scraped, check `process_start_time_seconds` to decide whether zero
initial value can be assumed for counters. This requires keeping metrics in memory until the entire
response is received.

options.name: exclude_labels
options.description:
A list of labels to be excluded. May be used in conjunction with `include_labels`.
Labels defined in `excluded labels` will take precedence in case of overlap.

options.name: include_labels
options.description:
A list of labels to include. May be used in conjunction with `exclude_labels`.
Labels defined in `excluded labels` will take precedence in case of overlap.

options.name: bearer_token_auth
options.description:
If set to true, adds a bearer token authentication header.
If set to 'tls_only', only adds a bearer token authentication header if the endpoint is secure https.
Note: If bearer_token_path is not set, the default path is /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token.

options.name: bearer_token_path
options.description:
The path to a Kubernetes service account bearer token file. Make sure the file exists and is mounted correctly.
Note: bearer_token_auth should be set to true to enable adding the token to HTTP headers for authentication.

options.name: bearer_token_refresh_interval
options.description: The refresh interval to keep the bearer token up-to-date.

options.name: ignore_metrics
options.description:
A list of metrics to ignore, the "*" wildcard can be used to match multiple metric names.
The wildcard matching is done via fnmatch, it locates a match anywhere in the string.

options.name: ignore_metrics_by_labels
options.description:
A mapping of labels where metrics with matching label key and values are ignored.
Use the "*" wildcard to match all label values.

options.name: ignore_tags
options.description: A list of regular expressions used to ignore tags added by autodiscovery and entries in the `tags` option.

options.name: proxy
options.description:
This overrides the `proxy` setting in `init_config`.

Set HTTP or HTTPS proxies for this instance. Use the `no_proxy` list
to specify hosts that must bypass proxies.

The SOCKS protocol is also supported, for example:

  socks5://user:pass@host:port

Using the scheme `socks5` causes the DNS resolution to happen on the
client, rather than on the proxy server. This is in line with `curl`,
which uses the scheme to decide whether to do the DNS resolution on
the client or proxy. If you want to resolve the domains on the proxy
server, use `socks5h` as the scheme.

options.name: skip_proxy
options.description:
This overrides the `skip_proxy` setting in `init_config`.

If set to `true`, this makes the check bypass any proxy
settings enabled and attempt to reach services directly.

options.name: auth_type
options.description:
The type of authentication to use. The available types (and related options) are:
```
  - basic
    |__ username
    |__ password
    |__ use_legacy_auth_encoding
  - digest
    |__ username
    |__ password
  - ntlm
    |__ ntlm_domain
    |__ password
  - kerberos
    |__ kerberos_auth
    |__ kerberos_cache
    |__ kerberos_delegate
    |__ kerberos_force_initiate
    |__ kerberos_hostname
    |__ kerberos_keytab
    |__ kerberos_principal
  - aws
    |__ aws_region
    |__ aws_host
    |__ aws_service
```
The `aws` auth type relies on boto3 to automatically gather AWS credentials, for example: from `.aws/credentials`. /noqa
Details: https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/guide/configuration.html#configuring-credentials /noqa

options.name: use_legacy_auth_encoding
options.description: When `auth_type` is set to `basic`, this determines whether to encode as `latin1` rather than `utf-8`.

options.name: username
options.description: The username to use if services are behind basic or digest auth.

options.name: password
options.description: The password to use if services are behind basic or NTLM auth.

options.name: ntlm_domain
options.description:
If your services use NTLM authentication, specify
the domain used in the check. For NTLM Auth, append
the username to domain, not as the `username` parameter.

options.name: kerberos_auth
options.description:
If your services use Kerberos authentication, you can specify the Kerberos
strategy to use between:

  - required
  - optional
  - disabled

See https://github.com/requests/requests-kerberos#mutual-authentication

options.name: kerberos_cache
options.description:
Sets the KRB5CCNAME environment variable.
It should point to a credential cache with a valid TGT.

options.name: kerberos_delegate
options.description:
Set to `true` to enable Kerberos delegation of credentials to a server that requests delegation.

See https://github.com/requests/requests-kerberos#delegation

options.name: kerberos_force_initiate
options.description:
Set to `true` to preemptively initiate the Kerberos GSS exchange and
present a Kerberos ticket on the initial request (and all subsequent).

See https://github.com/requests/requests-kerberos#preemptive-authentication

options.name: kerberos_hostname
options.description:
Override the hostname used for the Kerberos GSS exchange if its DNS name doesn't
match its Kerberos hostname, for example: behind a content switch or load balancer.

See https://github.com/requests/requests-kerberos#hostname-override

options.name: kerberos_principal
options.description:
Set an explicit principal, to force Kerberos to look for a
matching credential cache for the named user.

See https://github.com/requests/requests-kerberos#explicit-principal

options.name: kerberos_keytab
options.description: Set the path to your Kerberos key tab file.

options.name: auth_token
options.description:
This allows for the use of authentication information from dynamic sources.
Both a reader and writer must be configured.

The available readers are:

  - type: file
    path (required): The absolute path for the file to read from.
    pattern: A regular expression pattern with a single capture group used to find the
             token rather than using the entire file, for example: Your secret is (.+)
  - type: oauth
    url (required): The token endpoint.
    client_id (required): The client identifier.
    client_secret (required): The client secret.
    basic_auth: Whether the provider expects credentials to be transmitted in
                an HTTP Basic Auth header. The default is: false
    options: Mapping of additional options to pass to the provider, such as the audience
             or the scope. For example:
                options:
                  audience: https://example.com
                  scope: read:example

The available writers are:

  - type: header
    name (required): The name of the field, for example: Authorization
    value: The template value, for example `Bearer <TOKEN>`. The default is: <TOKEN>
    placeholder: The substring in `value` to replace with the token, defaults to: <TOKEN>

options.name: aws_region
options.description:
If your services require AWS Signature Version 4 signing, set the region.

See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html

options.name: aws_host
options.description:
If your services require AWS Signature Version 4 signing, set the host.
This only needs the hostname and does not require the protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, and more).
For example, if connecting to https://us-east-1.amazonaws.com/, set `aws_host` to `us-east-1.amazonaws.com`.

Note: This setting is not necessary for official integrations.

See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html

options.name: aws_service
options.description:
If your services require AWS Signature Version 4 signing, set the service code. For a list
of available service codes, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html

Note: This setting is not necessary for official integrations.

See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html

options.name: tls_verify
options.description: Instructs the check to validate the TLS certificate of services.

options.name: tls_use_host_header
options.description: If a `Host` header is set, this enables its use for SNI (matching against the TLS certificate CN or SAN).

options.name: tls_ignore_warning
options.description:
If `tls_verify` is disabled, security warnings are logged by the check.
Disable those by setting `tls_ignore_warning` to true.

options.name: tls_cert
options.description:
The path to a single file in PEM format containing a certificate as well as any
number of CA certificates needed to establish the certificate's authenticity for
use when connecting to services. It may also contain an unencrypted private key to use.

options.name: tls_private_key
options.description:
The unencrypted private key to use for `tls_cert` when connecting to services. This is
required if `tls_cert` is set and it does not already contain a private key.

options.name: tls_ca_cert
options.description:
The path to a file of concatenated CA certificates in PEM format or a directory
containing several CA certificates in PEM format. If a directory, the directory
must have been processed using the `openssl rehash` command. See:
https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.2/man1/c_rehash.html

options.name: tls_protocols_allowed
options.description:
The expected versions of TLS/SSL when fetching intermediate certificates.
Only `SSLv3`, `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3` are allowed by default. The possible values are:
  SSLv3
  TLSv1
  TLSv1.1
  TLSv1.2
  TLSv1.3

options.name: tls_ciphers
options.description:
The list of ciphers suites to use when connecting to an endpoint. If not specified, 
`ALL` ciphers are used. For list of ciphers see: 
https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.0.2/man1/ciphers.html

options.name: headers
options.description:
The headers parameter allows you to send specific headers with every request.
You can use it for explicitly specifying the host header or adding headers for
authorization purposes.

This overrides any default headers.

options.name: extra_headers
options.description: Additional headers to send with every request.

options.name: timeout
options.description:
The timeout for accessing services.

This overrides the `timeout` setting in `init_config`.

options.name: connect_timeout
options.description: The connect timeout for accessing services. Defaults to `timeout`.

options.name: read_timeout
options.description: The read timeout for accessing services. Defaults to `timeout`.

options.name: request_size
options.description: The number of kibibytes (KiB) to read from streaming HTTP responses at a time.

options.name: log_requests
options.description: Whether or not to debug log the HTTP(S) requests made, including the method and URL.

options.name: persist_connections
options.description: Whether or not to persist cookies and use connection pooling for improved performance.

options.name: allow_redirects
options.description: Whether or not to allow URL redirection.

options.name: tags
options.description:
A list of tags to attach to every metric and service check emitted by this instance.

Learn more about tagging at https://docs.datadoghq.com/tagging

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.

options.name: min_collection_interval
options.description:
This changes the collection interval of the check. For more information, see:
https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/write_agent_check/#collection-interval

options.name: empty_default_hostname
options.description:
This forces the check to send metrics with no hostname.

This is useful for cluster-level checks.

options.name: metric_patterns
options.description:
A mapping of metrics to include or exclude, with each entry being a regular expression.

Metrics defined in `exclude` will take precedence in case of overlap.
